sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax in Syracuse, NY?
sections.html:
The City Payment Center prepares the bill and takes payment for City, School and County property tax together, while the Department of Assessment sets the value. Both are in City Hall at 233 East Washington Street. The Payment Center is in Room 122, open Monday to Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and its phone is 315-448-8310. Assessment is in Suite 130 at 315-448-8270.

The Payment Center services more than 42,000 taxpayer accounts. It also enforces collection of delinquent property tax and handles the sale of tax-delinquent properties. Enter City Hall from the Market Street side, expect a security check, and know that on-street parking nearby is metered.

Syracuse is the Onondaga County seat. The Census Bureau counts 25.06 square miles of land, which works out to about 5,930 residents per square mile in 2020.

  • Payment Center: bills, payments, delinquent tax, tax trust payment plans.
  • Assessment: values, exemptions, change of address for notices, grievance forms.
  • Onondaga County Clerk: copies of deeds.

sections.h2: When are Syracuse property taxes due?
sections.html:
Ask the City Payment Center at 315-448-8310 for the due dates on your current bill. The same office can tell you what you owe today and whether any prior year is open. A tax question that lands at the Assessment office is routed to the Payment Center, which oversees taxes.

If the bill has gone to the wrong place, file a Change of Address for City Service Notifications with the Department of Assessment. That form covers tax bills, assessment notices and other property notices, so owners who have moved or inherited a house should file it before the next bill cycle.

Homeowners who have fallen behind can apply for a tax trust, which is the City's payment plan for delinquent property tax. The application is a PDF on the Payment Center page. Parcels that go through tax foreclosure are transferred to the Greater Syracuse Property Development Corporation, known as the Land Bank, and are then offered for sale there.

sections.h2: How do I challenge my Syracuse assessment?
sections.html:
File a formal grievance with the Board of Assessment Review during the last two weeks of January. The board is made up of four or five officers appointed by the City Council, and it can reduce an assessment for good cause. Grounds include an assessment that is unequal, excessive or unlawful, and a wrong property classification.

Fill out the grievance form, print it and sign it by hand. Bring or mail it to City Hall, Suite 130. The office accepts only forms with an original signature, complete documentation, and a filing date inside those two weeks. Forms that arrive early or late are not taken. The office has posted evening and Saturday-morning hours during the window.

New York State law requires assessors to hold every property at a uniform percentage of market value (RPTL sections 301 and 305). Syracuse assesses by cost, income and comparable sales, then adjusts for physical changes or market shifts. Each parcel has its own market value, which is why neighbors' assessments differ.

sections.h2: Why did my Syracuse tax bill go up, and who can explain a charge?
sections.html:
A bill rises when the assessment changes, an exemption status changes, the tax rate moves, or a special charge not tied to assessment is added or increased. That is the Department of Assessment's own list. If a charge on your bill is unfamiliar, call 315-448-8270 and staff will look into it.

Physical changes matter too. Building or tearing down a porch or garage can change an assessment to match the new value. Properties are valued by accepted real estate methods, which can include cost, income and comparable sales, with adjustments for physical changes or the market.

To find out who owns a parcel, the Department points to the SDG Image Mate lookup by address. It does not keep owner phone numbers. The City also maintains tax maps that show lot dimensions but not buildings, so a boundary question needs a private survey from the seller's files.

sections.h2: Which Syracuse tax exemptions can I claim, and by when?
sections.html:
Most exemptions require an application to the Department of Assessment before January 1, and the Department asks you to call or visit instead of downloading a form blind, because each exemption has its own form and supporting papers. The table summarizes what the City page says.

Syracuse property tax exemptions (source: City of Syracuse Department of Assessment)
ExemptionTaxes reducedKey rule
STARCity and SchoolRegistered with New York State; no yearly renewal
Senior citizenCity, School, CountyAge 64 or older, owned one year, income under $58,400; 5% to 65% sliding scale; renew yearly
VeteransCity and CountyDD-214 required; no yearly renewal
DisabilityCity, School, CountyIncome under $58,400, proof of disability; 5% to 50% sliding scale; renew yearly
Flood zoneCityProperty in one of two flood zone districts

A property cannot take both the senior and the disability exemption on one account. Renewal forms for the income-based programs are mailed each August and must be back before January 1. The Department also lists a historic property exemption and property improvement exemptions for renovating vacant, residential and commercial buildings.

sections.h2: What should I check before selling a Syracuse house with tax owing?
sections.html:
Get a written payoff from the City Payment Center and ask whether the County and School portions are included. The Payment Center collects all three, so one figure should cover them. Then confirm with your closing attorney that any tax trust balance is paid off at the closing table.

  • Ask the Payment Center whether the account is in a tax trust and what remains owing.
  • Get a copy of your deed from the Onondaga County Clerk, which keeps the official deed records.
  • Check the City's tax map of your parcel. It shows lot lines but not buildings, so a seller usually supplies a private survey.
  • If the exemption on your bill is a senior or disability exemption, tell the buyer it will not carry over.

Syracuse averages about 115.6 inches of snow a year, so ask your inspector to look closely at the roof, gutters and drainage before you list.

sections.h2: What do Syracuse housing numbers look like?
sections.html:
Syracuse is a city of renters. Census QuickFacts for 2020-2024 give an owner-occupancy rate of 41.6 percent, a median owner-occupied value of $138,400 and a median gross rent of $1,039. Median household income is $47,819. The 2020 census counted 148,620 people, and the July 2025 estimate is 144,896.

The Syracuse City School District covers the whole city and runs 34 schools plus four alternative programs. The city recognizes 26 neighborhoods, from University Hill and Tipperary Hill to the north and south sides, and it sits at the crossing of I-81 and I-90. Syracuse University and SUNY Upstate Medical University anchor the economy, and Micron began building a large chip complex in the northern suburbs in 2024.

faqs.q: Where do I pay my Syracuse property tax?
faqs.a: At the City Payment Center, Room 122 in City Hall, 233 East Washington Street, Monday to Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. It collects City, School and County tax in one place.

faqs.q: When is Syracuse Grievance filing season?
faqs.a: The last two weeks of January each year. The forms must be signed in ink and delivered to City Hall, Suite 130, inside that window.

faqs.q: Can I get a payment plan for back taxes in Syracuse?
faqs.a: Yes. The City Payment Center offers a tax trust for homeowners who have fallen behind. Pick up the application from the Payment Center page or call 315-448-8310.

faqs.q: Does the STAR credit lower a Syracuse bill directly?
faqs.a: Only for owners registered before 2015. Newer registrants get a credit check or direct deposit from New York State, which they use to pay City and School tax.

faqs.q: What happens to a Syracuse house after tax foreclosure?
faqs.a: It is transferred to the Greater Syracuse Property Development Corporation, the Land Bank, which lists available properties for sale.
